speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please tell me your age and specifically what antibiotic you were prescribed before developing this fever, rash, and joint pain. This history is crucial for determining if this is a drug reaction.

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) / Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN).

Based on the timing of the rash appearing one week after starting amoxicillin, the initial involvement of the antecubital and popliteal fossae, and the presence of fever, joint pain, and an itchy rash spreading to the trunk, the clinical picture strongly suggests a severe cutaneous adverse reaction (SCAR). I need to evaluate the extent of skin detachment and mucosal involvement immediately. REQUEST IMAGES: Full body dermatology photos focusing on the palms, soles, and mucous membranes (mouth, eyes, genitals). REQUEST TEST: Skin biopsy.
